title: The Fifth-Floor Kingdom
summary: Carrie finally gets the five displaced Norse adults to apartment 5B; Bjorn judges the small hall while Gunnar immediately reads the building as a place people actually live.
settingText: Bushwick apartment building stairs and fifth-floor landing

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building stairs and fifth-floor landing
panelPlan.action: Carrie climbs the last narrow flight with the scratched brass key and a thin DTI folder; Bjorn, Gunnar, Astrid and the two male Kin follow with their remaining bags and bundled possessions.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building stairs and fifth-floor landing
panelPlan.action: Carrie unlocks 5B. Bjorn looks past her into the cramped studio.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building stairs and fifth-floor landing
panelPlan.action: The three Kin enter without ceremony and begin setting down bedding and bags while Gunnar studies the hall and stairwell.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building stairs and fifth-floor landing
panelPlan.action: Carrie points the key at Gunnar without slowing.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment building stairs and fifth-floor landing
panelPlan.action: Bjorn rests one hand on the doorframe, evaluating the threshold rather than the size.

dialogueInline.text: Fifth floor. No elevator. I fought for the window.
You fought for this room?
I fought a housing spreadsheet. It was uglier than you think.
One stair. One hall. Two ways out.
Please do not start with ways out.
A hall is judged first by its doors.

title: One Very Efficient Room
summary: The household begins making the studio usable before Carrie can finish explaining it, establishing that settlement is already a shared practical job rather than a caseworker lesson.

panelPlan.action: Full room geography: entry door, kitchenette/table, radiator, main window with fire escape, sleeping area. Astrid checks the sink; First Male Kin moves a chest against the wall; Second Male Kin opens the main window; Gunnar clocks the fire escape.
Bjorn turns slowly in the center of the one-room studio.
Astrid turns the cold tap; water runs. First Male Kin tests the table. Second Male Kin looks out at the alley.
Gunnar points through the open window to the iron fire escape.
Carrie sees where his attention went.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. Temporary housing. How temporary is still apparently a mystery.
This is one room.
Legally, one very efficient room.
The window has a road.
Emergency exit. We are not using it recreationally.

title: Walls Carry Water
summary: Hot water and reliable indoor heat land as ordinary modern miracles, while Carrie sees the group responding through practical curiosity rather than spectacle.

panelPlan.action: Astrid turns the hot tap; steam begins to curl from the chipped sink.
Gunnar puts two fingers under the water, then follows the pipe with his eyes into the wall.
Bjorn looks from the hot tap to the radiator.
The three Kin exchange a quiet look at the running water, then return to unpacking rather than gathering around it.
Bjorn says it as an observation, not praise.

dialogueInline.text: Hot.
The wall carries water.
Who keeps the fire?
The building. Mostly.
Your city hides labor in walls.
And sends a bill later.

title: Hunger Has Arrived
summary: The first domestic problem is not a form but dinner; Carrie's inability to feed five people from her emergency bag pushes the household into the neighborhood.

panelPlan.action: Carrie opens a small DTI emergency grocery bag on the table: crackers, two protein bars, bottled water, almost nothing for six adults.
Bjorn looks into the bag with restrained disbelief.
Gunnar is already at the window, looking down at the storefronts and awnings on the block.
Astrid lifts the empty bread cloth from their travel bag; First Male Kin taps an equally empty food pouch.
Carrie grabs her coat and DTI badge.

dialogueInline.text: Okay. This is not dinner.
You brought us to a hall without stores?
There are stores below.
Fine. Field trip. Nobody buys a sword.

title: The Store Downstairs
summary: Carrie takes the entire household to the bodega, where the first neighborhood relationship begins with groceries, practical indifference, and the fact that Bjorn still has no usable money.

panelPlan.action: All five displaced adults enter the compact bodega with Carrie. The owner glances up, then keeps ringing a regular customer.
Astrid and the two male Kin stay together choosing bread, eggs, fruit and packaged food while Gunnar studies handwritten price cards.
Bjorn places a small piece of hacksilver on the counter beside the groceries.
The owner looks at the silver, then at Carrie.
Carrie pays from her own wallet while Bjorn watches the transaction with visible discomfort.
The owner bags the groceries and slides the hacksilver back without comment.

dialogueInline.text: Door closes behind you.
For the food.
Cash or card.
Neither. Yet.
I am putting this on the growing list of things you owe me.
Name the debt.
Come back when your money works.

title: First Meal
summary: The first meal makes the room feel less temporary, and Carrie learns that she does not have to teach every piece of modern domestic life for the household to use it.

panelPlan.action: Back in 5B, Astrid watches Carrie light the ordinary gas or electric burner once; the two male Kin lay out bread and groceries; Gunnar clears a stable work surface.
Astrid takes over the pan without hesitation while Carrie steps back.
Bjorn opens a paper-wrapped package and smells it before eating.
The six sit or lean wherever the cramped room allows, sharing the first ordinary meal in 5B.
Carrie realizes everyone is eating and nobody is asking what to do next.

dialogueInline.text: Low heat. Pan stays on the burner. Nothing else becomes a hearth.
The downstairs man sells good salt.
Okay. That part was easier than intake.

title: The Iron Stair
summary: After the meal Gunnar tests the apartment's most tempting boundary: the fire escape, which Carrie defines as shared safety infrastructure rather than household territory.
settingText: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Gunnar opens the main window and steps one boot onto the fire escape landing while Bjorn looks over his shoulder.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Astrid and the two male Kin remain inside near the sill, passing Gunnar a coil of cord he had left by the window.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Carrie appears behind them with the placement folder still under one arm.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks down through the iron grid to the alley.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio main window and fire escape
panelPlan.action: Gunnar looks toward the next roof, where pigeons have gathered.

dialogueInline.text: It holds weight.
Emergency exit. Not porch. Not watchtower. Not extra apartment.
Then it is a road for danger.
Exactly. Which is why we keep it boring.
Boring may be difficult.

title: The Bird Is Not Dinner
summary: A small pigeon snare turns the abstract idea of shared space into a real neighborhood boundary, while Silas first appears as an annoying witness rather than a season-long antagonist.
settingText: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window
panelPlan.action: A simple cord snare on the fire escape has caught one ordinary pigeon by the leg without injuring it; Gunnar crouches near it while Bjorn evaluates the bird.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window
panelPlan.action: Silas records vertically from the adjacent fire escape, fascinated.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window
panelPlan.action: Carrie reaches the window, sees both the pigeon and Silas.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window
panelPlan.action: Gunnar loosens the cord while Bjorn tests the rule.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick fire escape and apartment window
panelPlan.action: The pigeon flies off. Silas lowers the phone only slightly.

dialogueInline.text: Caught.
Small.
Please tell me that is not dinner.
Release the bird.
You forbade hunting on shared ground.
Everything outside this window is shared enough to get us evicted.
Shared boundary.
Good. Keep that one.

title: The Neighbor Knocks
summary: The first conflict with a real neighbor ends through ordinary reciprocity rather than Carrie winning an argument, giving the household its first social foothold in the building.

panelPlan.action: The Upstairs Neighbor stands at 5B holding a length of cord that had fallen across her section of the fire escape.
Carrie starts an apology while Bjorn steps forward.
Astrid appears beside Bjorn with one unopened packaged snack from the bodega and offers it to the neighbor without a speech.
The neighbor looks at the snack, then at Astrid, and takes it.
The door closes. Carrie looks at Astrid.

dialogueInline.text: This yours?
Yes. Sorry. It is gone now.
The boundary was unclear.
No ropes on my window. We are good.
That was either an apology or a treaty.
It worked.

title: The Paper Returns
summary: With the household fed and the immediate neighbor problem settled, Carrie returns to the placement acknowledgement and discovers that Bjorn's objection is not to the terms but to pretending literacy he does not possess.

panelPlan.action: Night begins outside. Carrie clears a corner of the table and reopens the placement packet while the three Kin organize bedding behind her.
Bjorn sits opposite her. Gunnar remains nearby, repairing the cord from the fire escape.
Carrie points to the signature line.
Bjorn looks at the printed page rather than the pen.
Carrie stops treating the signature as routine.

dialogueInline.text: One more thing before I leave.
We judged the rules.
And this says you agreed to them.
I agreed to what you told me. I will not mark words I cannot judge.
Okay. That's different.

title: What Does the Mark Prove?
summary: Carrie's obvious workaround fails because copying a signature would make Bjorn perform knowledge he does not have, and Gunnar reframes the procedural problem around truthful consent.

panelPlan.action: Carrie writes BJORN on scrap paper and slides it across.
Bjorn studies the letters.
Carrie gestures from the sample to the signature line.
Gunnar rotates the packet so the signature box faces him.
Carrie looks at the exact wording instead of answering automatically.

dialogueInline.text: You could copy your name here.
Those are your strokes.
They become yours if you make them.
Then I would swear I know what I do not know.
Does the box require his name, or his agreement?
It says signature.
That was not my question.

title: Night Work
summary: While the household quietly becomes livable around them, Bjorn sees that Carrie is still working because the incomplete file can threaten a home that already feels real.

panelPlan.action: The room is dimmer and calmer. Astrid folds bedding; First Male Kin organizes food on one shelf; Second Male Kin places tools away from the door. Carrie is still at the table searching DTI guidance.
Bjorn watches Carrie rub her eyes and reopen another page.
Carrie keeps reading.
Bjorn looks around at the already functioning room.
Behind them, Gunnar deliberately keeps the exit path clear while the Kin finish setting sleeping places.

dialogueInline.text: Why do you remain?
Because if this file stays incomplete, somebody tomorrow can decide the placement is incomplete.
The hall is here.
I know. Paper can be slow to notice.

title: The Call
summary: DTI confirms that actual compliance is not enough without a valid acknowledgement, making the bureaucratic pressure precise and limited instead of consuming the whole issue.

panelPlan.action: Carrie's phone is on speaker beside the packet.
Carrie gestures around the lived-in studio as if the supervisor could see it.
Bjorn listens without interrupting.
Bjorn looks at Carrie.

dialogueInline.text: The placement still has no executed acknowledgement.
They accepted the terms. They are following the terms.
I am not disputing behavior. I need a valid acknowledgement in the file.
Without the mark, the hall is not ours.
Without a valid mark, the system refuses to say it is.

title: The Household Already Exists
summary: Carrie searches for another legal route while the household independently organizes itself around the very safety and tenancy obligations the form is supposed to document.

panelPlan.action: Gunnar and the two male Kin shift a chest away from the exit path; Astrid stores food away from the radiator; Bjorn relocates his own gear when Gunnar points to a safer place.
Carrie scans the acknowledgement rules at the table, barely looking up.
First Male Kin tests the door swing after moving the chest.
Bjorn looks from the room to Carrie's paperwork.
Carrie's finger stops on a footnote.

dialogueInline.text: Door path stays empty.
Correct. Surprisingly correct.
Clear.
Tell your paper to look up.
Wait.

title: Find the Hinge
summary: Carrie finds a witnessed-mark exception and turns obscure procedure into a truthful way to record Bjorn's agreement.

panelPlan.action: Carrie calls DTI again with the footnote open.
The supervisor answers through the phone.
Carrie taps the word REQUIRED in the guidance.
Bjorn listens, interested in the distinction.

dialogueInline.text: I found a witnessed-mark exception. It does not say the mark has to be a conventional signature.
The Department strongly prefers conventional signatures.
Preferred is not required.
Your law contains a door.
Most laws do. The trick is finding the hinge.

title: The Bloodless Pact
summary: Bjorn accepts a witnessed thumbprint because it records the agreement he actually made without asking him to imitate modern literacy.

panelPlan.action: Carrie places a black ink pad beside the form.
Gunnar studies the size of the box.
Bjorn inks one thumb.
The thumbprint lands squarely in the witnessed-mark field.
The three sit with the completed paper between them while the rest of the household continues ordinary evening tasks behind them.

dialogueInline.text: No blade?
No blade.
The whole hand would be stronger.
The city does not need your whole hand.
Witness it.
I witness it.

title: PROVISIONAL
summary: DTI accepts the witnessed mark and provisional placement, and the comic relief comes from the fact that the household has already been unpacking for hours.

panelPlan.action: Carrie sends the completed form from her phone or laptop.
Gunnar looks around at the thoroughly rearranged room.
Phone confirmation from the DTI supervisor.
Bjorn checks the exact meaning.
Astrid and the two male Kin pause amid bedding, groceries and tools already in place.

dialogueInline.text: Nobody touch anything for ten seconds.
That instruction arrived late.
Conditional placement accepted. Review remains pending.
We may remain.
You may unpack.
We did.

title: The Brass Key
summary: Carrie finally gives Bjorn the apartment key, converting provisional status into a concrete responsibility he understands.

panelPlan.action: The scratched brass key rests in Carrie's palm.
Bjorn takes it carefully.
Bjorn looks toward the door, then the window.
Gunnar points to the lock.
Bjorn closes his hand around the key.

dialogueInline.text: Now you get this.
The brass key.
It grants command of the walls?
It opens the front door. The roof remains very much not yours.
It bars others as well as us.
Then it is a serious thing.

directionInline.text: Use the same ordinary scratched brass apartment key established throughout the issue.

title: What Rent Buys
summary: Bjorn accepts rent more readily when Carrie explains it as reciprocal obligation rather than tribute, and Gunnar converts the apartment into a two-sided household ledger.

panelPlan.action: Carrie writes RENT and FIRST OF MONTH on a scrap beside the placement packet.
Bjorn looks unimpressed.
Carrie points around the room.
Gunnar writes a short list of both sides of the exchange.
Bjorn accepts the formulation.

dialogueInline.text: Next problem: rent.
Tribute to the one who owns the walls.
In exchange: heat, water, a roof, a door that locks, and repairs when the building breaks.
We owe money. He owes the hall.
Then count both.

title: Their Order
summary: The household decides how to inhabit the room; Carrie enforces only actual safety limits while Astrid and the two male Kin begin to read as separate practical people within the group.

panelPlan.action: Astrid chooses the food shelf and cooking area; First Male Kin claims a dry corner for folded bedding; Second Male Kin arranges the small tools near the table; Gunnar marks the clear door path.
Bjorn starts to move First Male Kin's bedding, then stops when the man moves it back himself.
Carrie points only to the blocked sprinkler pipe.
The room changes through several small choices rather than one command.
Bjorn hangs the brass key on a simple hook near the door.

dialogueInline.text: Nothing hangs from that. Everything else, negotiate among yourselves.
Then this is our order.

title: The Radiator Knocks
summary: A harmless radiator knock lets the household test its new ordinary competence and gives Bjorn one sincere compliment for modern domestic life.

panelPlan.action: The old radiator clangs sharply.
Astrid and the two male Kin look up; Gunnar crouches and checks the pipe without touching the valve.
Carrie listens once.
The heat continues. Everyone returns to what they were doing.
Bjorn holds his hands near the radiator.

dialogueInline.text: The wall is loud.
Air in the radiator. Annoying, not dangerous.
It heats the room while we sleep?
That is the dream.
Your age has done some things well.

title: Tomorrow's List
summary: Carrie leaves emergency contacts and a practical tomorrow list, while the bodega receipt and household groceries quietly establish that neighborhood life has already begun.
settingText: Bushwick studio table near the door

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table near the door
panelPlan.action: Carrie writes three numbers on a card: building super, DTI after-hours, her office.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table near the door
panelPlan.action: Gunnar puts the contact card beside the bodega receipt and his small household map.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table near the door
panelPlan.action: Astrid puts the remaining bread away while the two male Kin settle bedding.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table near the door
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks at the groceries, then the contact card.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio table near the door
panelPlan.action: Bjorn nods as if she has just described two separate campaigns.

dialogueInline.text: If the building fails, call the super. If DTI fails, call after-hours. If all else fails, call me.
Same marks. Different doors.
Tomorrow we buy food without your money.
Eventually. First I teach you the train. Then we get you money that stores recognize.

title: Lock It Behind Me
summary: Carrie leaves the functioning household and tells Bjorn to lock her out, making privacy and the turn of the brass key the final practical lesson of the night.
settingText: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway
panelPlan.action: Carrie stands in the open doorway with coat and folder; the household remains inside the organized studio.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway
panelPlan.action: Bjorn follows her to the threshold.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway
panelPlan.action: Carrie points to the brass key in his hand.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks from Carrie to the hallway.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway
panelPlan.action: From inside 5B, the brass key turns in the lock after Carrie steps into the hall.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick studio doorway and fifth-floor hallway
panelPlan.action: Bjorn tests the locked handle once. Behind him Gunnar sits with the household map while Astrid and the two male Kin continue separate small tasks.

dialogueInline.text: I am leaving before something else becomes municipal.
And tomorrow?
Tomorrow you still live here.
Lock it behind me.
You give a hall and command us to bar you from it.
That is privacy. You are going to love it.
She cannot enter without us opening it.
Good.

title: Landfall
summary: The issue closes on a warm, functioning household whose ordinary routines now matter more than the form that made the placement provisional.
settingText: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior
panelPlan.action: Inside 5B: bedding arranged, groceries put away, household map, completed packet, bodega receipt, contact card and brass key all coexist in one coherent room.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior
panelPlan.action: Astrid stores the last food while First Male Kin settles folded bedding and Second Male Kin checks the window latch; no one waits for Bjorn to assign them places.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior
panelPlan.action: Bjorn looks at the key hanging by the door.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior
panelPlan.action: Gunnar glances at the review notice still clipped to the packet.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior
panelPlan.action: The radiator heats the small room while street light crosses old Norse travel gear and new bodega groceries.

panelPlan.location: Bushwick apartment 5B late night and hallway exterior
panelPlan.action: In the hallway outside the locked door, Carrie leans briefly against the wall, hears ordinary movement inside, then heads for the stairs.

dialogueInline.text: Ours under law.
Until the review.
Then we make the time count.
Please just make it to morning.
